atoms.a:
The students in class 5B put all their rulers in a line. There are 30 students in class 5B and each ruler is 30 cm long.

How long is the line of rulers?

atoms.b: The line of rulers is <mat><gap>900</gap></mat> cm long, which is equivalent to <mat><gap>9</gap></mat>m.
atoms.sound: The line of rulers is 900 cm long, which is equivalent to 9 metres.

atoms.a:
Each house on Leo’s street has 33.25`m` of fence. There are 12 houses on Leo’s street.

How many metres of fence are there in total? Convert the length to centimetres to avoid multiplying with decimals.
atoms.sound: Each house on Leo’s street has 33.25 metres of fence. There are 12 houses on Leo’s street.How many metres of fence are there in total? Convert the length to centimetres to avoid multiplying with decimals.

hint.text: Don’t forget to convert back to metres!

atoms.b: There are <mat><gap>399</gap>`m`</mat> of fence on Leo’s street.
atoms.sound: There are 399 metres of fence on Leo’s street.

atoms.a:
Luis and his friend are playing with a toy racetrack. Luis wants the cars to travel a total of 25 m.

How far is this in centimetres?
atoms.sound:
Luis and his friend are playing with a toy racetrack. Luis wants the cars to travel a total of 25 metres.

How far is this in centimetres?

atoms.a: If one lap has a length of 50 cm, what division would you have to do to find out the number of laps needed?
How can this division be simplified?

atoms.b: They would have to finish <mat><gap>50</gap></mat> laps to reach a distance of 25 metres.
